drafts.title: $0 USPS redelivery fee, so that text is fake
drafts.angle: Black Friday orders ship today and fake package-on-hold texts come right behind them. One rule people remember, plus how he checks a weird text. Different from his WhatsApp/Telegram group warning yesterday.
bullets: USPS does not charge a redelivery fee; its tracking texts only come if you signed up, and they have no links (FCC; Fox News citing USPS).
Forward suspicious texts to 7726 (SPAM); emails to spam@uspis.gov (FCC).
Fake package delivery problems were the most reported text scam in 2024 (FTC, cited by Fox News).

Non-payment and non-delivery scams cost people more than $503 million last year (FBI IC3, FBI Boston, Nov 24, 2026). New twist: texts saying your order is stuck in customs until you pay a tariff (FCC).
drafts.body: $0. That's what USPS charges to redeliver a package. So the text saying I owe {$X} to release my Black Friday order? Fake. Real USPS tracking texts don't even have links. I forward those to 7726 and {how I check a weird text first}. Gotten one yet? 📦
drafts.framework_body:
$0. That's what USPS charges to redeliver a package.

So the text saying I owe {$X} to release my Black Friday order? Fake.

Real USPS tracking texts only come if you signed up. And they don't have links.

The new one going around says your package is stuck in customs until you pay a tariff. Also fake.

What I do: forward it to 7726, delete it, and check the order in the store's own app. {how I check a weird text first, like pasting it into Grok and asking if it's real}

These scams took more than $503 million from people last year.

If you've got parents who shop online, send them this one.

Gotten one yet? 📦

drafts.title: 50 MW: who pays for data center power on the Xcel bill (policy)
drafts.angle: Colorado regulators decide before year end how 50 MW+ customers like data centers pay for the lines and plants they need. His line: let tech pay its own way, not my bill.
bullets: Colorado PUC finished the evidentiary hearing on Xcel's Large Load Tariff, Proceeding 26AL-0137E (PUC November newsletter, Nov 10).
It sets how customers needing 50 MW or more pay for transmission, substations, interconnection upgrades and new generation built for them.
A decision hearing is to be scheduled before the end of the calendar year.
Separately, Xcel's 2027-2028 resource adequacy plan has a proposed settlement, also up for decision before year end.
